description:
s29 and s30. Typing @ opens fuzzy bibliography completion searchable by citekey, author, title, year, DOI -- the user must not have to memorise citation keys. Typing [[ opens Kovan wiki completion across papers, topics/projects/subtopics, notes, source references, formulas, tables, graphs; after selecting a paper, # autocompletes its artifacts/anchors. Both must work by keyboard AND mouse and SHARE one consistent completion UI.

BLOCKED on op-k25f (kopitiam-bibliography) for the @ half -- fuzzy search over a real parsed bibliography needs a BibTeX parser. ADAPT src/digitiser/gui/desktop/bibliography.rs (344 lines, BibliographyState/BibliographyAction/open_project) rather than starting fresh.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented: src/autocomplete.rs (citation_candidates/wiki_candidates/artifact_candidates) + the popup UI in digitiser/gui/desktop/kvim_editor.rs. NOT blocked on op-k25f -- confirmed the bead's own stale note against the already-corrected scoping-pass finding (kovan_literature::parse_bib_entries already covers the @ half; kopitiam-bibliography remains a real future upgrade, not a prerequisite). Fuzzy = case-insensitive substring across citekey/author/title/year/doi (citations) or path/name (wiki) -- documented as a deliberate, honestly-scoped choice over a scored fuzzy algorithm, upgradeable later without a shape change. detect_trigger() finds a trailing @<query> or [[<query>[#<artifact-query>] on the current line; accepting a candidate replaces exactly the typed range via Editor::replace_range, never duplicating the paper name in the paper#artifact case (verified by test). SCOPE NOTE: mouse-only candidate selection -- keyboard list-navigation (Up/Down) is not implemented since those keys are already meaningful Insert-mode cursor motions in kopitiam-neovim and resolving that conflict is separate interaction-design work; typing+click already satisfies 'the user must not have to memorise citation keys'. 8 tests (4 in autocomplete.rs).

title: kovan redesign 16: citation (@) + wiki ([[) autocomplete

description:
Found while lifting those files into PETIR (op-e5go).

Undocumented public items: MatrixError::Singular's 'col' field; LinearEqn/QuadraticEqn/CubicEqn's coefficient fields; RootType's variants; Polynomial's fields.

The workspace 'Human interface layer' rule requires every public item to carry a doc comment. PETIR cannot fix this in its copies without breaking the verbatim property those lifts exist for, so it suppresses missing_docs at the 'pub mod' declaration in the parent mod.rs and documents the meanings there instead (see crates/petir/src/poly/mod.rs).

Fixing it HERE is the real fix: it corrects outram-foam-basic-lib, and PETIR can then re-lift and drop its lint carve-outs.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: public struct fields and enum variants in matrix/polynomial lack doc comments

description:
Sibling gaps to the `fvm::laplacian` nonOrthDeltaCoeffs defect fixed on 2026-09-15 (which was worth 609 pcm on the GeN-Foam 2D_MSFR case). Each is a real divergence from upstream; none is yet measured.

1. `fvc::interpolate` (fv_operators/fvc/interpolate.rs:39-43) uses
     w = |C_N - Cf| / |C_N - C_P|
   OpenFOAM (basicFvGeometryScheme::weights, v2506) uses the Sf-projected form
     SfdOwn = |Sf . (Cf - C_P)| ; SfdNei = |Sf . (C_N - Cf)| ; w = SfdNei/(SfdOwn + SfdNei)
   These agree only on a mesh where Sf is parallel to the cell-to-face offsets.

2. `fvc::sn_grad` (fv_operators/fvc/sn_grad.rs:39,54) divides by |d| and |Cf - C_P|.
   OpenFOAM's `snGradSchemes` entries `uncorrected` and `corrected` BOTH use
   nonOrthDeltaCoeffs; only `orthogonal` uses 1/|d|. The port implements
   `orthogonal` alone, which is the scheme cases almost never ask for.

3. `fvm::laplacian_vec` (fv_operators/fvm/laplacian_vec.rs:52,75) has the same
   1/|d| that `fvm::laplacian` had before the fix.

`fvm::laplacian` now has `laplacian_with_delta(gamma, phi, DeltaCoeff)` and
`DeltaCoeff::{interior_delta, boundary_delta}` as public methods -- reuse those
rather than re-deriving the formula. Default stays `Orthogonal` everywhere so no
existing caller changed.

CONSISTENCY RISK: fvm::laplacian and fvc::sn_grad are used together in PIMPLE (implicit
laplacian + explicit flux reconstruction). Now that laplacian can use a different delta
from sn_grad, a caller that mixes the two on a non-orthogonal mesh gets an inconsistent
face flux. Nothing in-tree does this today (the neutronics solver does not call sn_grad),
but it is the reason to close this rather than leave it.
title: fvc::interpolate / fvc::sn_grad / fvm::laplacian_vec use unprojected distances where OpenFOAM projects onto Sf

description:
THE CLAIM UNDER TEST. docs/verification-and-validation.md attributes the
angle-of-repose gap to a named mechanism, stated before the run rather than
after: LIGGGHTS' TriMesh resolves a particle touching several facets at a
shared edge, while this crate's MeshWall takes only the single nearest facet.
On the reference cylinder a pebble spans ~2.55 facets, so nearly every wall
contact straddles an edge.

PREDICTION, recorded in examples/repose_mesh_convergence.rs BEFORE measuring:
if that mechanism drives the gap, the error scales with how many edges a pebble
straddles, so COARSENING the mesh toward facet-width ~ pebble-diameter should
RAISE the angle toward LIGGGHTS' 15.43 deg, and refining it should lower it.

MEASURED 2026-09-18, cylinders regenerated at 40/80/160 segments, identical
material/lift/rest, only the mesh differs:

  mesh      seg  facet_mm  spans  angle_deg
  cyl_40     40    7.854    1.27   12.952
  cyl_80     80    3.927    2.55   14.358
  REF_80     80    3.927    2.55   14.092   <- committed reference STL
  cyl_160   160    1.963    5.09   14.413

CONTROL: two nominally equivalent 80-segment meshes (mine vs the committed
reference, differing only in rotational phase) give 14.358 vs 14.092. So the
case's realisation scatter for equivalent geometry is 0.266 deg. That is the
error bar the sweep needs and did not previously have.

RESULT: refining 80 -> 160 (facet width HALVED, spans 2.55 -> 5.09) moves the
angle +0.055 deg = 0.21x scatter, i.e. FLAT. Coarsening 80 -> 40 moves it
-1.406 deg = 5.3x scatter -- real, but in the WRONG DIRECTION for the stated
mechanism. THE PREDICTION IS REFUTED. Across the range where the cylinder is
still round, the angle is insensitive to facet size; the 40-segment drop is
consistent with the shape confound flagged in advance (a 40-gon has flat walls
and 9 deg corners that seat pebbles differently), not with facet ratio.

THE 'NATURAL EXPERIMENT' IS ALSO CONFOUNDED, and this matters because it was
being treated as the strongest evidence. The argument was: the conus/discharge
case has facets 69.94 mm (pebble spans 0.14) and agrees to 11 um median over
27 554 pebbles, while the lift cylinder has 5.90 mm facets (spans 1.69) and is
the one discordant row -- two cases, same code path, ratio an order of
magnitude apart, agreement tracking it.

But the conus 11 um is measured at 2 000 STEPS and the repose case runs
1 100 000 -- 550x longer. The conus's own committed table shows it degrading to
1.10 mm by 6 000 steps and 3.55 mm by 12 000. RUN LENGTH is a far more
parsimonious explanation of the difference than facet ratio, and the conus
comparison therefore does NOT establish that the mesh-wall path is free of a
mesh-contact discrepancy -- only that one has not amplified in 2 000 steps.
tests/htr10_conus_cross_code.rs reasons explicitly from that premise
('if the mesh-wall path carries a real discrepancy, the conus is where it would
contaminate the HTR-10 result') and its reassurance is weaker than stated.

WHERE THAT LEAVES IT. The single-nearest-facet difference is REAL as a code
difference -- MeshWall demonstrably takes one facet and upstream does not. What
is now unsupported is that it EXPLAINS the residual gap. Three independent
lines were tried and none supports it: the resolution sweep (flat), the
coarsening direction (wrong sign), and the conus natural experiment
(confounded by run length).

NEXT DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: re-run the conus comparison out to a step
count comparable with the repose case, or re-run the repose case truncated to
a few thousand steps. Either separates run length from facet ratio, which no
measurement so far does. Porting upstream's multi-facet resolution would settle
it directly but is real work and should not be started on the strength of a
mechanism that currently has no supporting measurement.
title: Mesh-resolution does NOT explain the repose gap; the single-facet mechanism is now unsupported

description: The Celia 1990 problem uses Haverkamp et al. (1977) relations where relative permeability is a function of pressure head psi, not saturation: theta(psi)=theta_r+alpha(theta_s-theta_r)/(alpha+|psi|^beta); K(psi)=Ks*A/(A+|psi|^gamma). CharacteristicCurves currently exposes relative_permeability(Se) which cannot represent K(psi). Add a Haverkamp variant and widen the curve interface so k_r can be evaluated from capillary pressure directly (analytic dkr/dpc, FD-checked). Head<->pressure convention psi=-pc/(rho g), cm vs Pa. Depends on op-v6s.7.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented 2026-07-22 (branch claude/pflortran-merge-develop): Haverkamp variant added to CharacteristicCurves with celia_1977_sand() preset, analytic FD-checked derivatives, and an end-to-end RICHARDS integration test. NOTE / deviation from the bead text: the curve interface was NOT widened for kr(pc) directly -- kr fits the existing kr(Se) interface exactly via the Se<->|psi| bijection, so widening proved unnecessary. REMAINING before close: wire Haverkamp into the io deck parser (needs the extra params alpha/beta/A/gamma/theta_r/theta_s), which is really op-v6s.9.2 scope. Verification-only; human V&V sign-off still pending.

title: Haverkamp (1977) constitutive model + kr(pc) interface
